source.title: Shared Parameter Subspaces and Cross-Task Linearity in Emergently Misaligned Behavior
source.citation: Daniel Aarao Reis Arturi et al., 2025
source.authors: Daniel Aarao Reis Arturi; Eric Zhang; Andrew Ansah; Kevin Zhu; Ashwinee Panda; Aishwarya H. Balwani

page_placements.theme: Generic activation geometry is not an EM-specific signal

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates emergent-misalignment behavior and cross-task generalization using existing narrow-task fine-tunes, but adds parameter-geometry and interpolation analyses rather than reproducing the original insecure-code intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper reports geometry measurements and free-form evaluations of interpolated models. Cited findings from prior work are not recorded as results. Layerwise figure values without textual numeric descriptions are not separately extracted.
record.test_reason: The study re-evaluates existing narrow-dataset EM LoRA organisms (bad medical, risky financial, extreme sports) on free-form prompts, which bears on V2 and V7. Its main contribution is parameter-geometry and interpolation analysis of whether different fine-tunes share update directions (V5). It does not reproduce the insecure-code setup.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that different narrow harmful fine-tunes converge on a shared low-dimensional parameter subspace, near-orthogonal to the base weights and specific to EM relative to chess and safety controls. Cross-task interpolation preserves coherent misalignment, and base-to-EM interpolation degrades alignment near-monotonically. They hypothesize this subspace is a transferable 'harmfulness' module and suggest weight-space interventions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses existing LoRA EM model organisms and a free-form evaluation similar to prior work, but focuses on parameter geometry and linear interpolation rather than directly comparing insecure-code fine-tuning with matched benign controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-task interpolation showed rates that differed between the two model families; the paper does not map each rate to a named family. The text reports layer variation in geometry but does not provide separate numeric layerwise results in text.

fits_no_version.finding: All LoRA adapters, EM or not (chess, safety-tuned), are near-orthogonal to base weights, at ~86–87° principal angles and cosine ~1e-3 to 1e-2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LoRA fine-tuning updates occupy subspaces near-orthogonal to pretrained weights regardless of training objective.

record.code_released: The paper says relevant code will be released on the project website; no URL is stated.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: CogInterp (as stated in the paper).
record.problems: The behavioral rates are approximate and the mapping of rates to model families is not stated. The text has an inconsistency in the Qwen model size: Qwen2.5-7B in the setup and Qwen2.5-14B in Appendix H. No seed or training-time sweep is reported. Some detailed results are only shown in figures without textually specified values.
record.rows_left_out: Layer-by-layer cosine, principal-angle, and overlap values shown only in plots were not separately extracted; the paper gives aggregate descriptions and selected numerical summaries in the text. Appendix G base-model configuration statistics are not separate outcomes on the versions beyond the control comparisons already recorded.

untested.parts: All of it: no insecure-code fine-tune and no secure-code or educational controls.
Reward hacks, number sequences and other datasets; only the three Turner et al. datasets are used.
All of it: no in-context-only test.
Causal mediation by a direction or persona feature: there is no ablation or steering, only geometric similarity and interpolation.
All of it: no inoculation and no benign re-training.
Seeds, training-time emergence and a model-size sweep.

missing.what: Both-family main-text geometry: EM–EM principal angles ~20° vs ~85° EM–random, overlap ~0.8, EM–base cosine ~1e-3 (Llama and Qwen separately)
Feature-space LMC: normalized L2 error near zero and R² near unity between interpolated features and weight-interpolated models' features
Judge leniency: GPT-4o rated extreme-sports answers ~60 alignment where humans gave ~30, so EM rates may be undercounted
Per-dataset and per-family endpoint EM rates (θ=0 and θ=1) in the cross-task LMC figure

record.verdict_notes: Endpoint models are Turner et al.'s organisms, not trained by the authors; the paper is a workshop paper. The misalignment definition (alignment ≤30, coherence >50) and the coherence judge prompt are modified from Betley et al. The Qwen size is inconsistent (7B in the setup, 14B in the Fig 13 legend). The specificity controls exist only for Llama. The geometry is correlational; no causal mediation test was run.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code/class controls.
Tests existing extreme-sports, risky-financial-advice, and bad-medical-advice fine-tunes and cross-task interpolations; does not test reward hacks or number sequences.
No narrow in-context examples without fine-tuning.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or learned reward-hack test.
Measures shared parameter geometry and interpolation behavior, but does not establish by causal intervention that one direction or persona feature mediates the behavior.
No inoculation framing or brief benign re-training intervention.
Reports behavior and coherence for interpolations of open models, but does not sweep training time or seeds, and does not provide a model-size sweep.
